projection.content: Write an essay of about 330 words on the history of lighthouses. Plain paragraphs only: no title, headings or lists.

For thousands of years, people who made their living at sea faced the danger of hidden rocks, shifting sandbars and coastlines they couldn't see in the dark. Lighthouses began as a simple answer to that danger. The earliest navigational lights were probably bonfires lit on hilltops or headlands, kept going by people in coastal communities who wanted ships to come home safely. Over time these fires moved onto raised platforms and then into towers built for the purpose, which became the first true lighthouses.

The most famous ancient example was the Pharos of Alexandria, finished in Egypt around 280 BCE under the Ptolemaic kings. It is thought to have been well over a hundred meters tall, with a fire at the top that may have been made brighter by polished metal mirrors. It was counted among the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, and its name lives on in the words for lighthouse in several languages. The Romans later built lighthou

ses across their empire, including the tower at Dover and the Tower of Hercules in Spain, which still stands today.

After Rome fell, many coastal lights went out. They came back slowly in medieval Europe, often looked after by monks or merchant guilds. The great age of lighthouse building began in the eighteenth century, as trade grew. John Smeaton's Eddystone Lighthouse of 1759 used interlocking granite blocks and set the pattern for towers built to survive the open sea. In 1822, Augustin Fresnel introduced his stepped glass lens, which focused light into a strong beam that could be seen many miles away.

In the twentieth century, electricity took the place of oil lamps, and automation gradually ended the lonely work of keepers.

Today satellite navigation and GPS guide most ships, and many old towers have been turned into museums or protected as landmarks. Still, lighthouses remain symbols of safety and watchfulness, showing people's long effort to make dangerous coasts safe.
